(By Sri. N Mahesh Prasad, Adv.,)
 JUDGMENT

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.90,00,000/- on account of the death of K Khadervalli, in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:
On 31-10-2023 at about 11.30 a.m., the deceased was proceeding by riding his Hero Honda Splendor + motor cycle bearing No. TN.23.AV.0770 near Kushi Dhaba Hotel on Palamaner to Punganur road, Panjani Mandal and at that time the driver of XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679 driven the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner towards Palamaner side, lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased from opposite direction and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body and died on the spot.

Thereafter body was shifted to Government hospital, Punganuru, wherein postmortem was conducted and handed over the body to the petitioners and they have performed funeral and obsequies ceremonies by spending an amount of Rs.2,00,000/-.

Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy aged about 54 years and was running Rakvalli Bar and family restaurant and also doing agricultural work and thereby earning Rs.80,000/- p.m. and contributing his entire earnings to the maintenance of the family.
Due to the untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically, they have lost their bread earner.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679
are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.90,00,000/- with interest.

Reshma .K vs Prabhakar Reddy .R on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198061146/
2 3.
After service of notices, both the respondents appeared through their counsel, but respondent No.1 owner has not filed written statement.

Respondent No.2 insurance company filed its written statement by admitting issuance of policy to the XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further it has denied the cause and manner of accident and also involvement of the offending car in the alleged accident.

Further contended that the owner of the offending car has entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having valid driving license as on the date of accident and hence violated the policy conditions.
Further it has denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The compensation as claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant and fanciful.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition against it.
4.
On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased K Khadervalli, died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 31-10-2023 at about 11.30 a.m. near Kushi Dhaba hotel, Panjani, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh Kaiwara cross, Chintamani taluk,
Chikkaballapura due to the rash and negligence driving of the Car bearing No.
AP.39.MV.1679 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the first petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.
Inspite of sufficient opportunity the respondents have not chosen to lead evidence.
6. Heard the arguments.
Perused the material evidence that is available on record.

At the time of arguments it is found that in the issue No.1 the address of Chintamani taluk, Chikkaballapura is wrongly mentioned by oversight, hence, by removing the same the issue No.1 is reframed as follows:
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased K Khadervalli, died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 31-10-2023 at about 11.30 a.m. near Kushi Dhaba hotel, Panjani, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligence driving of the Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679 by its driver?

Reshma .K vs Prabhakar Reddy .R on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198061146/
3 7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.
Issue No.1: In the affirmative

,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.4: As per final orders  for the following.-
 REASONS ISSUE NO.1:
8.

The petitioners to prove their claim have produced true copies of FIR, complaint,
rough sketch, IMV report, AIR report, inquest report, PM report, case dairy and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 9.
9.

As per the documents, Ex.P1 FIR is came to be registered on the basis of the first information given by one Sampalle Jakeer Hussain, who is the son of deceased as per Ex.P2 by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679.
The Ex.P1 and P2 are in consonance with the contents of petition wherein they have alleged about the negligence of driver of XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679.
In continuation of the investigation the IO has conducted rough sketch as per Ex.P3.
On perusal of Ex.P3 the accident spot is in the left side portion of the road in which the deceased was proceeding in his motorcycle.
The offending car bearing No.AP-39MV-1679 which was coming from Palamaner towards Punganur came to the wrong side i.e., extreme right side and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.
Thus, the contents of Ex.P.3 discloses the actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing No.AP-39MV-1679 who came to his extreme right side/wrong side and caused the accident.
If the driver of car bearing No.AP-39MV-1679 proceeded in his way i.e., in his left side portion of the road the said accident was not going to be caused.

10. At the time of cross-examination of PW1 the learned counsel for the respondent No.2-insurance company has taken contention that the accident was in the middle of the road and as it is head on collision there was a negligence from the part of the deceased.

But the said contention cannot be acceptable, because as per the Ex.P3 rough sketch the accident spot is not in the middle of the road,
but accident spot is in the left side portion of the road which evidentiates that the driver of car bearing No.AP-39MV-1679 came to his wrong side.
As such no grounds are made out to consider the contributory negligence.
11. Further the Ex.P4 is the IMV report wherein the car bearing No.AP-39MV-1679 has got damages in its front windshield, front bonnet and front right side dom bumper got scratches.

The contents of Ex.P3 rough sketch & Ex.P4 IMV report establishes that the driver of the XUV 700 Car bearing No.
AP.39.MV.1679 came from opposite direction ie., to his wrong side of the road and caused the accident.
This shows that the driver of XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679 was negligent and caused the accident by coming to his wrong side.

The contents of rough sketch and IMV reports Reshma .K vs Prabhakar Reddy .R on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198061146/
4

prima facie establishes the negligence of the driver of XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679.
12.
In the accident cases, it is settled principle of law that "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" which means the things speaks itself, is the standing principle to know the nature of the accident.
Under this principle how the negligence has to be infer is considered.

In tort law, "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" principle that allows petitioners to meet their burden of proof with under which a court can infer negligence from the very nature of an accident or injury in the absence of direct evidence on how any defendant behaved in the context of tort litigation.

On perusal of Ex.P3- rough sketch along with Ex.P4 IMV report wherein the damages of the vehicles involved in the accident is mentioned prima- facie shows the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679.
Hence, by applying the said principle the negligence on the part of the driver of offending XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679 is stands established.

The Ex.P3 rough sketch being the self explanatory established the negligence on the part of the driver of offending XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679.
13.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
14. Even here in this case the driver XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679 is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the offending XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679 and he was charge sheeted as per Ex.P9.
15.

In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of offending XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679 resulting in the death of Sri K Khadervalli.
16.

The injuries sustained by the deceased is mentioned in Ex.P6 inquest and Ex.P7 postmortem,
which also evidentiates the nature of the accident and injuries sustained and also the death by the deceased due to the injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident.

Ex.P9 is the charge sheet filed Reshma .K vs Prabhakar Reddy .R on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198061146/
5 against the driver of the offending XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679 for the offence punishable under Sec. 304-A of IPC.

The investigating officer as per Ex.P9 charge sheet opined that the driver of offending XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679 driven the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident.
17. The respondents have not lead any evidence.

It is very important to note that as per Ex.P3 rough sketch, the accident has occurred in the left side portion of the road, which in turn proves before this tribunal that there was no contribution on the part of the deceased, even though he was riding the motor cycle.
During the course of cross-examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioner.
18. As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.

Looking to the oral as well as documentary evidence of the petitioners there are sufficient materials to show that Sri K Khadervalli died in the accident dated 31-10-2023 which is caused by the driver of the XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679.
Accordingly issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 19.

As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that K Khadervalli died on 31-10-2023 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the driver of respondent No.1.
20.
As contended in the petition the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children of the deceased K Khadervalli.
The respondents do not specifically deny the relationship of petitioners with deceased.
The petitioners to prove their relationship with the deceased, have produced the notarized copies of Aadhar cards of petitioners which are marked under Ex.P14.

During the course of recording the evidence the notarized copies of Aadhar cards are compared with the original documents and found correct.
21.

As per these documents the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 to 4 are children of deceased K Khadervalli but the respondents do not dispute the relationship of the petitioners with deceased.
The respondents do not dispute the Aadhar cards produced by the petitioners.
The respondents have not adduced any evidence to disprove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.

22. At the time of cross-examination the contention is raised by the respondent No.2 insurance company that the petitioner No.3 is the married daughter and the petitioner No.2 & 4 being the major sons are not entitled for compensation.

23. In this regard, in the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356 between National Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s. Birender and others, wherein it is held as follows;
"A claim petition filed by major married and earning sons of the deceased mother,
the Honourable Supreme Court held as follows:
Reshma .K vs Prabhakar Reddy .R on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198061146/
6 "12.

entities.text: National Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s. Birender and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166 (1).
The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependent on the deceased would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.

This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra)
had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
"It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependant on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

The evidence on record in the present case would suggest that the claimants were working as agricultural labourers on contract basis and were earning meagre income between Rs.1,00,000/ and Rs.1,50,000/ per annum.
In that sense, they were largely dependant on the earning of their mother and in fact, were staying with her, who met with an accident at the young age of 48 years".

The judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.102868/2014 between Reliance General Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa and others held as follows:
"Having considered the principles laid down in the judgements referred to supra, this Court has taken note of recent judgement of the Apex Court in Birender, wherein it is held that even married sons are entitled for compensation not only on conventional heads but also on loss of dependency.

entities.text: Reliance General Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the very contention of the appellant-insurance company cannot be accepted.

26. This Court also would like to rely upon the judgement of the Division Bench of this Court in MFA No.118/2018 dated 26.03.2021, wherein also this Court by relying upon the judgement in Birender, held that even married sons are also entitled for compensation not only on conventional head but also on loss of dependency''.
In the High Court of Punjab and Hariyana at Chadigarh in FAO No.1007 and 1008 /2014 dated 10-02-2020 between Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Vipanjit Kaur and others "No doubt, the son is aged around 48 years and working in the Air Force while the daughter is aged around 42 years and her husband is posted as a Sub Inspector in the Punjab Police and both of them are thus having their own independent sources of income.

entities.text: High Court of Punjab and Hariyana at Chadigarh
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Vipanjit Kaur and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short, 'the Act') admittedly is a welfare statute for the betterment of the claimants.
No doubt, both the claimants are grown up and self-dependent but that does not mean or can be construed that they did not suffer any loss on account of sudden loss of both of their parents.

It has been rightly Reshma .K vs Prabhakar Reddy .R on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198061146/
7 contended by learned counsel for the respondents/claimants that son and the daughter with the death of their parents have lost protection, physical as well as psychological, besides sense of fulfillment of having parents to look after and cater to their daily requirements of life and emotional support.

No doubt, the parents were senior citizens but one has to take a realistic approach that they would certainly be looking after their grand-children for their nurturing, psychological and physical well-being, and would be a source of joy and happiness for the entire family.
By this loss the family has lost companionship, and the pain and agony that has accompanied this sudden loss can never be compensated in terms of money.
One cannot ignore the fact that Surinder Kaur even in her advance age would be contributing her lot in the household chores, cooking food, cleaning and such like daily duties.

The family claims to be having agricultural land besides having milching cattle and therefore, in rural household it is a matter of common knowledge that women contribute towards looking after the cattle and agricultural produce and contribute their lot towards the source of earning from these fields.

The learned Tribunal has lost sight of the fact in not awarding compensation on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, which are handsomely part of calculations in such claim petitions.

Since there is no division of heads under which various amounts of compensation has been awarded, but having an overall look at the total compensation awarded in case of each of the deceased being ` 4.52 lacs and ` 3.50 lacs in lump sum and considering what has been left out as detailed in the foregoing lines, keeping in view the prevalent price index, there is no overwhelming occasion for this Court to show indulgence and thus this Court does not feel that the amount so awarded could be in any manner termed to be excessive necessitating intervention by this Court and rather appears to be just and appropriate in the prevalent scenario.
In the light of the same, the impugned award does not call for any interference and both the present appeals as such are disposed of as dismissed.
On the same point of law in the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Kerala reported in 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others).

entities.text: 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held in this case, the earning sons are also dependents and also entitled compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act.

24. Further with regard to the married daughters right of claiming compensation in the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in AIR 2007 SC 1474 in the case of Manjura Beri V. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Wherein it was held that even a married daughter can seek compensation.

entities.text: Manjura Beri V. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 25. On the same point of law in the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru in MFA No.2332/2013(MV-D) in the case of Dr. Amrutha @ Amruthavathi V/s Chavalla Kumar Raja Naidu & another it is held that, even the major children can claim the compensation.

entities.text: Dr. Amrutha @ Amruthavathi V/s Chavalla Kumar Raja Naidu & another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 26. By applying the above precedent merely because the petitioner No.3 is the married daughter and petitioner No.2 & 4 being the major sons of the deceased their application cannot be rejected.

In this case also, as per the evidence available on record the deceased was running Rakvalli Bar and Family Reshma .K vs Prabhakar Reddy .R on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198061146/
8 Restaurant and also was doing agricultural work.

entities.text: Rakvalli Bar and Family Reshma .K vs Prabhakar Reddy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, they are certainly dependents on each other.
Accordingly, in this case the petitioner No.2 to 4 being a major sons and daughter are entitled for the compensation in accordance with their dependency.
Accordingly, issue No.2 answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE No.3 27.

As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that K Khadervalli died on 31-10-2023 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by the driver of Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679.
28.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.
As per Ex.P.7 - PM report, deceased was aged about 54 years.
If it is considered, as on the date of the accident the age of the deceased was 54 years.
29. As stated in the petition deceased was running Rakvalli Bar and Family Restaurant and was also doing agricultural work and earning Rs.80,000/- per month.
To prove the said fact, the petitioners have produced Ex.P15 RTC's and Ex.P16 Noukar Nama.
The Ex.P.16
even though establishes that the deceased was working as supplier in Rock Valley Bar and Restaurant, no other evidence is placed to establish the income of the deceased.
The owner of the said shop or the account statement of the deceased is not produced to show the income of the deceased.

Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2023.
30.
As per Sarala varma case the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 11.

Since the deceased left his wife and children, it is considered that, there are four dependents of deceased,
hence 1/4th is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then the total loss of dependency would be (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 11 = Rs.21,12,000/- minus 1/4th (Rs.5,28,000/-) = Rs.15,84,000/-.
31.

In Civil Special leave petition (Civil No.25590/2014 dated 31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "While determining the income, in case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

Once notional income is determined,
the effects of inflation would equally apply.
Further, no one would ever say that the improvements in skills that come with experience do not take place in the domain of Reshma .K vs Prabhakar Reddy
.R on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198061146/
9 work within the household.

It is worth nothing that, although not extensively discussed, this Court has been granting future prospects even in cases pertaining to notional income, as has been highlighted by my learned brother, Surya Kant, J., in his opinion (Hem Raj V. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, (2018) 15 SCC 654:
Sunita Tokas V. New India Insurance Company Ltd., (2019) 20 SCC 688)".
33.

entities.text: Hem Raj V. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, (2018) 15 SCC 654
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sunita Tokas V. New India Insurance Company Ltd., (2019) 20 SCC 688)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As per the above decisions 10% out of loss of dependency has to be granted towards future prospects which would Rs.1,58,400/-.
34.
The Petitioners are the wife and children of the deceased Khadervalli.
The petitioners are the wife and children of the deceased and they lost their loving care taker.

Therefore they are entitled to a sum of Rs.1,76,000/- (Rs.44,000/each. Rs.40,000/x 10% hike every three years from 2017 as per Pranay Sethi Case) under the head of loss of consortium., Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).

The petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1.Loss of dependency Rs. 15,84,000/-
2. Loss of future prospects Rs. 1,58,400/-
3. Loss of consortium Rs. 1,76,000/-
4. Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500/-
5. Transportation of dead body Rs. 16,500/ Total Rs. 19,51,400/-
35. Liability:-
The respondent No.2 insurance company in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679.

Even though the respondent No.2 insurance company has taken contention that the driver of the offending Car bearing No.
AP.39.MV.1679 was not having valid driving license at the time of accident, but no evidence is placed in this regard and the police has also not invoked any provisions or penal sections against the driver of offending Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679 in the charge sheet for driving the said vehicle without having license.
No other grounds are made out to show the violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 - owner.
Hence, the said defence of the respondent No.2 insurance company cannot be acceptable.

Accordingly, the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the liability of respondent No.1 owner and they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, this issue answered partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4:-
36.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
Reshma .K vs Prabhakar Reddy .R on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198061146/
10 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.19,51,400/- (Rupees Nineteen lakh fifty one thousand four hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioners No.1 to 4 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 70:10:10:10.
The respondent No.2 insurance  company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of awarded amount of petitioner No.1 50% shall be released to petitioner No.1 on her proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in her name in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years.
The entire compensation amount of petitioner No.2 to 4 is directed to be release in their favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In tort law, "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" principle that allows petitioners to meet their burden of proof with under which a court can infer negligence from the very nature of an accident or injury in the absence of direct evidence on how any defendant behaved in the context of tort litigation.
On perusal of Ex.P3- rough sketch along with Ex.P4 IMV report wherein the damages of the vehicles involved in the accident is mentioned prima- facie shows the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679.
Hence, by applying the said principle the negligence on the part of the driver of offending XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679 is stands established.
The Ex.P3 rough sketch being the self explanatory established the negligence on the part of the driver of offending XUV 700 Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679.
13.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
During the course of cross-examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioner.
18. As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.
The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short, 'the Act') admittedly is a welfare statute for the betterment of the claimants.
No doubt, both the claimants are grown up and self-dependent but that does not mean or can be construed that they did not suffer any loss on account of sudden loss of both of their parents.
No doubt, the parents were senior citizens but one has to take a realistic approach that they would certainly be looking after their grand-children for their nurturing, psychological and physical well-being, and would be a source of joy and happiness for the entire family.
By this loss the family has lost companionship, and the pain and agony that has accompanied this sudden loss can never be compensated in terms of money.
One cannot ignore the fact that Surinder Kaur even in her advance age would be contributing her lot in the household chores, cooking food, cleaning and such like daily duties.
The family claims to be having agricultural land besides having milching cattle and therefore, in rural household it is a matter of common knowledge that women contribute towards looking after the cattle and agricultural produce and contribute their lot towards the source of earning from these fields.
Since there is no division of heads under which various amounts of compensation has been awarded, but having an overall look at the total compensation awarded in case of each of the deceased being ` 4.52 lacs and ` 3.50 lacs in lump sum and considering what has been left out as detailed in the foregoing lines, keeping in view the prevalent price index, there is no overwhelming occasion for this Court to show indulgence and thus this Court does not feel that the amount so awarded could be in any manner termed to be excessive necessitating intervention by this Court and rather appears to be just and appropriate in the prevalent scenario.
On the same point of law in the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Kerala reported in 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others).
24. Further with regard to the married daughters right of claiming compensation in the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in AIR 2007 SC 1474 in the case of Manjura Beri V. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Wherein it was held that even a married daughter can seek compensation.
Accordingly, in this case the petitioner No.2 to 4 being a major sons and daughter are entitled for the compensation in accordance with their dependency.
Even though the respondent No.2 insurance company has taken contention that the driver of the offending Car bearing No.
AP.39.MV.1679 was not having valid driving license at the time of accident, but no evidence is placed in this regard and the police has also not invoked any provisions or penal sections against the driver of offending Car bearing No. AP.39.MV.1679 in the charge sheet for driving the said vehicle without having license.
No other grounds are made out to show the violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 - owner.
Hence, the said defence of the respondent No.2 insurance company cannot be acceptable.
